name: Features
summary: Eleven features sections for the AhaSlides marketing sites (Webflow Features), in the layouts of the Untitled UI features sections the marketing team picked: alternating rows, an icon grid, icon lists with a photo or a video, icon cards, icons around a phone or a results screenshot, and tabs with screenshots. Framework-free HTML and CSS, bound to the shared --aha-* tokens and built from values the Hero, Cards, Hero banner, FAQ and Footer banner sections already ship. Every picture is a neutral image slot to swap for a real image.
highlights: Eleven layouts on one page, each with its own labelled preview and paste-and-run snippet
Layout copied from Untitled UI; every colour, size, space, radius and font is an --aha-* token, and the eyebrow, title, lead and buttons carry the Hero section's values verbatim

Every picture is an image slot (4:3, 16:9 or portrait 3:4, the Cards and Hero banner ratios) with a neutral placeholder to swap for a real image; no third-party photo or device image, and no product recreated in HTML
Icon squares are the DS Feature card icon; the Learn more link is the Feature card link
Icon cards reuse the DS Feature card from the Cards page unchanged; this page adds only the grid around it
Icons are registry glyphs called by name with <aha-icon>
Tabs with screenshots ships working WAI-ARIA tabs (arrow keys, Home, End) in a short framework-free script; the structure maps onto Webflow's native Tabs element
The video variant is a poster slot with a play button and never autoplays
Each section is a container-query block: it steps down at 991 px and 767 px and tightens again below 480 px, wherever it sits

layouts.name: Alternating with screenshots
layouts.summary: A centred header, then three rows that swap sides: icon, title, text and two buttons beside an image. Each image slot is a neutral 4:3 placeholder to swap for a real product screenshot.
layouts.html:
Features

Everything you need to run a room that talks back

Polls, quizzes and word clouds your audience answers from their phones, and results you can see the moment they do.

  • Ask a question, see the room answer

    Put a live poll on any slide. Answers land as your audience votes, so you can react while the moment is still there.

    Demo Learn more

  • Turn answers into a word cloud

    Ask for one word and watch the most common answers grow. A quick way to take the temperature of a room of two or two hundred.

    Demo Learn more

  • Make quizzes people want to win

    Score points for speed and accuracy and show a leaderboard after every question. Teams, solo play and instant rematches included.

    Demo Learn more

layouts.name: Alternating with photos
layouts.summary: A centred header, then full-bleed rows that swap sides: icon, title, text and a check list beside a 4:3 photo that runs to the edge of the page. The photo is a neutral placeholder to swap for a real image.
layouts.html:
Features

See what the room thinks, as it happens

Start from a template or from scratch. Your audience joins with a code, no sign-up.

  • Live polls on any slide

    Ask a question and watch the answers arrive. Keep every voice in the room, not just the confident few.

    • Ask live polls and quizzes from any slide
    • Answers appear the second people submit
    • Download every response as a report

  • Questions without the awkward silence

    Let people post questions as they think of them, upvote the best and answer them when you are ready.

    • Anonymous or named questions
    • Upvotes sort the list for you
    • Moderate before anything shows on screen

  • Results you can act on

    Every session ends with a report of who answered what, so the next meeting starts from what you learned.

    • Per-question and per-person results
    • Export to Excel or PDF
    • Share a link with people who missed it

layouts.name: Tabs with screenshots
layouts.summary: A left-aligned header, a vertical list of tabs on the left and a 4:3 image slot on the right. Selecting a tab swaps the image. The tab rail follows the DS Tabs left rail (2px rule, primary when selected). Working WAI-ARIA tabs: arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs, and a short framework-free script ships in the snippet. The tab list and panels map one to one onto the Webflow Tabs element (Tab Menu and Tab Content).
